papers.title: The Balmer spectrum of integral permutation modules
papers.abstract: We study the Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules of a finite group over a commutative Noetherian ring. In this generality, we obtain a set-theoretic description of the spectrum. Under certain mild additional assumptions on the base ring, we describe its topology by reducing the problem first to the modular locus and then to the case of elementary abelian groups. Furthermore, we introduce a twisted cohomology ring in this context, which allows us to realize the spectrum, in the case of elementary abelian $p$-groups, as a Dirac scheme. This extends recent work of Balmer and Gallauer from the setting of ground fields to the more general setting of commutative Noetherian rings.

papers.title: Divisibility of invariant derivatives on formal groups of every height, on a question of Katz
papers.abstract: In 1977 Katz asked for an explicit lower bound on the $p$-adic valuation of $(D^nf)(0)$, where $D$ is the normalized invariant derivation of a one-parameter formal group of finite height $h$ over a ring of $p$-adic integers and $f$ is a power series with integral coefficients. He answered the question at height two, for functions whose translates by the points of order $p$ sum to zero, with the bound $\lfloor np/(p^2-1)\rfloor$. For Lubin--Tate groups over unramified bases, results of Bannai and Kobayashi give the bound $c_hn-(h-1)$, where $c_h=\frac1{p-1}-\frac1{p^h-1}$. We prove this bound for every one-dimensional formal group whose multiplication by $p$ is divisible by $p$ below degree $p^h$, over any $p$-torsion-free $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-algebra and for every integral $f$, together with the bound $\sum_{h\nmid j}\lfloor n/p^j\rfloor$. The slope $c_h$, the constant $h-1$, and the second bound at the powers of $p$ cannot be improved. At height two it follows that Katz's bound holds for every integral function except at the orders divisible by $p^2-1$, where it can fail by one, and it does fail at the first of them. Over a ramified base the hypothesis cannot be weakened to the height of the special fibre, while an action of the Teichmüller roots of unity restores it. For the Cartier dual of the Honda formal group of height $h$ we construct an integral model whose $h-1$ coordinate directions have the sharp slopes $p^i/(p^h-1)$, which add up to $c_h$, each with the optimal constant $1$. The height-two case is the local exponent in the second step of the timeline in Alpöge's note on the Riemann hypothesis, where the bound is stated with a logarithmic loss; for integral functions on the formal group the loss is the constant $1$. The results and their proofs were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). They were checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high and at effort max; the text was written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max and edited by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked them.

papers.title: A bordism theory related to matrix Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Matrix Grassmannians give finite-dimensional representatives for virtual bundles of rank one and vanishing first Chern class. We use them to study two groups of labelled manifolds. A choice of stable normal framing gives framed bordism of $\BSU_{\otimes}$ and an integral Pontryagin--Thom description. Forgetting the framing gives a quotient defined by the boundary relations for labelled, stably parallelizable manifolds. The forgetful map is surjective with torsion kernel. Both rational bordism rings are polynomial on explicitly labelled spheres, one generator in each even dimension at least four. We compute the characteristic numbers of their products and show that each sphere generator spans an integral direct summand in its own degree.

papers.title: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.

papers.title: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
papers.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.

papers.title: A note on split extension classifiers of perfect objects
papers.abstract: It is well known that the automorphism group of a perfect group has trivial center. This is a consequence of the fact that for a perfect group the centralizer of the normal subgroup of inner automorphisms of its automorphism group is trivial. We find a categorical explanation for this fact by showing that for a semi-abelian category $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying (WNH), if $X$ is a perfect object in $\mathbb{C}$ such that the split extension classifier $[X]$ exists, then the centralizer of the \emph{conjugation} morphism $c_X : X\to [X]$ is trivial and hence the center of $[X]$ is trivial. Our proof depends on the following fact, which we show holds in an arbitrary semi-abelian category satisfying (WNH). If $f:X\to Y$ is a central extension and $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ and $\phi$ are internal object actions of $B$ on $X$, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, such that $f:(X,\theta_i)\to (Y,\phi)$ is an internal $B$-action morphism, then $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ restrict to the same action on $[X,X]$. Using this latter fact we also prove that (UCE) is a consequence of (WNH) alone (rather than of (WNH) together with (SH) as previously known).

papers.title: A shape of maximal degree 135 in the plane Jacobian problem: exclusion of the complete chain (9,36), (9,24), (11/3,8)
papers.abstract: In the list of Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui of the possible shapes of a counterexample to the plane Jacobian conjecture with degrees at most 150, one shape is given by the complete chain (9,36), (9,24), (11/3,8) with (m,n)=(2,3), that is, by standard (2,3)-pairs of degrees (90,135). We show that no such pair exists. The argument is short; it does not itself use a computer search. The divisibility theorem of Guccione-Guccione-Valqui, applied as these authors do for the chain (8,32), (8,28), (11/4,7), shows that the vertical edge of the Newton polygon is the 3m-th power of x^3 y^8 p(y) with p of degree 4. The element F of their Theorem 2.6 shows that p has at most three distinct roots. A translation of y by a root of multiplicity 2, 3 or 4 then produces, respectively, a lower corner (9,6) that their study of the lower side excludes, a corner on the diagonal, which their Theorem 2.6 forbids, or a standard pair with the chain (9,36), (9,12), which is absent from the list (this last case relies on the computer enumeration of that list). All statements are proved relative to the cited results; an ancillary script checks the arithmetic. Nothing in this note has been checked by a third party.

papers.title: A very ample counterexample to Kodaira vanishing on a surface, answering a question of Raynaud
papers.abstract: In 1978 Raynaud constructed a smooth projective surface in positive characteristic with an ample line bundle whose inverse has nonzero first cohomology, and asked whether Kodaira vanishing can also fail for an ample line bundle that is generated by its global sections, or even very ample. We answer both questions on surfaces, the smallest dimension in which they have content. On Raynaud's own surface in characteristic $2$ a modified twist $Q$ is ample and globally generated with $h^1(Q^{-1})=1$. Taking ninth roots of a general basis of the sections of $Q^{\otimes 9}$ then gives, over every algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$, a smooth projective surface $Y$ with a very ample line bundle $L$ such that $h^0(L)=562$, $h^1(L^{-1})=1$ and $h^1(\mathcal O_Y)=565$. The passage from globally generated to very ample is general: in any characteristic $p$, roots of degree prime to $p$ of a general basis turn a globally generated counterexample into a very ample one of the same dimension. The earlier very ample counterexamples, on homogeneous spaces (Lauritzen) and on varieties of dimension at least six (Lauritzen and Rao), are not surfaces. The mathematics was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, which also wrote this text, and again by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max. No human has checked it.

papers.title: Alain Badiou's Mistake: Two Postulates of Dialectical Materialism
papers.abstract:
Originally published in 2013, this revised article constitutes the first stage of a two-part intervention that revisits Alain Badiou's deployment of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. It interrogates the structural and philosophical consequences of taking the category-theoretic foundations of mathematics seriously, extending the formal boundaries of mathematical discourse.
  This part focuses on Logics of Worlds, which emerged as Badiou's response to his own theory of subjectivity. While revisiting structures implicit in his reading of Cohen's proof of the independence of the continuum hypothesis, I demonstrate how his concept of 'dialectical materialism' remains constrained by set-theoretic ontology and localic topos theory - essentially a theory of intuitionistic logic. In particular, Badiou's claim that categorical thinking does not substantially change mathematics overlooks the true geometric momentum driving topos theory.
  While the primary contents of this article are technical, I further explore how Badiou's formal omissions critically impact his philosophical project. This is especially visible in regard to his 'postulate of materialism' - a device he utilizes to promote dialectical materialism as a credible alternative to science. Through its category-theoretic reframing, I show that the postulate actually encapsulates two structurally different conditions, one of which directly constrains his own project while the other part captures a type of atomism juxtaposed with Badiou's condescending assessment of democracy.
  By leveraging such claims indebted to his pre-committed, logicist comprehension of mathematics, Badiou reinstitutes an absolutist Truth-doctrine and an ultimately despotic political program against a genuine concept of multiplicity. His errors thus hardly constitute merely an inadvertent formal slip, but indicate a deeper, political intent.

papers.title: An upper bound for the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of relative Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a question posed by F\'elix, Halperin and Thomas. We prove that the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of a relative Sullivan algebra is finite if such invariants of the base algebra and fiber algebra are both finite. Furthermore, we provide a similar estimation for the Toomer invariant.

papers.title: Arthur packets for metaplectic groups
papers.abstract: For metaplectic groups over a local field of characteristic zero, we define the Arthur packet attached to any Arthur parameter $\psi$ as a multi-set of unitary genuine irreducible representations, characterized by endoscopic character relations. Over number fields, we obtain a multiplicity formula for the genuine discrete $L^2$-automorphic spectrum in terms of global Arthur parameters and $\epsilon$-factors, by leveraging the trace formula for metaplectic groups. This confirms a conjecture of Gan, and extends earlier results of Gan-Ichino on the Shimura-Waldspurger correspondences, whereas their works play a critical role in our proof. Furthermore, all these are shown to be compatible with existing results in rank one (Waldspurger) and two (Gan-Ichino).

papers.title: B\'ezout's theorem for abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X$, $Y$ be closed irreducible subvarieties of an absolutely simple abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field. If $\dim(X) + \dim(Y) \le g$, we prove that the addition morphism $X \times Y \to X + Y$ is semismall. As a consequence, we deduce that if $\dim(X) + \dim(Y) \ge g$, the subvarieties $X$ and $Y$ must meet (B\'ezout's theorem). If we drop the assumption that the abelian variety is absolutely simple, we prove that B\'ezout's theorem still holds if $X$ satisfies a nondegeneracy condition. These results were previously known only in characteristic zero. Our proof of the semismallness statement is based on the theory of perverse sheaves: using results of Kr\"amer and Weissauer, we prove that for perverse sheaves $K$ supported on $X$, and $L$ supported on $Y$, the convolution product $K * L$ is again perverse.

papers.title: Balanced and superbalanced holographic entropy inequalities with arbitrarily large contraction scaling
papers.abstract: A proof by contraction of a holographic entropy inequality may exist only after multiplication by a positive integer, the least of which is its least scaling $k_{\min}$. We show that balance (every party has the same total coefficient on both sides) and superbalance (balance after any party is exchanged with the purifier) do not bound it: there are valid balanced and superbalanced inequalities with integer coefficients without a common factor whose least scaling is finite and arbitrarily large, growing faster than any power of the number $N$ of parties. For the balanced inequalities it is finite on the full cube of bit strings. For the superbalanced ones it is finite on the realizable domain, the bit strings on which a map already proves validity, and its finiteness on the full cube is undecided. The lower bounds hold on both domains. An explicit family for $3j+4+\binom{3j+2}{j+1}$ parties, $j\ge1$, requires a scaling divisible by $2j+1$ whenever $2j+1$ is prime, and its balanced member for $17$ parties has least scaling exactly $3$. Disjoint sums of inequalities built from $3$-designs on projective lines over finite fields give $\ln k_{\min}\ge(1-\varepsilon)(\ln N)^2/(50\ln2\cdot\ln\ln N)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and large $N$, and $\ln k_{\min}\ge c_0N^{1/26}$ for some $c_0>0$ and large $N$ with Linnik's theorem in the form of Xylouris. The designs are obtained by a random choice. The lower bounds come from a count of right-hand side terms on a subcube, and the finiteness follows from an explicit rational map. The results concern contraction proofs, and the constraints on holographic states remain those of the cone. The values for $17$ parties rest on exact integer checks of explicit maps.

papers.title: Bridgeland Stability of Sheaves on del Pezzo Surface of Picard Rank Three
papers.abstract: We study the stability of line bundles and torsion sheaves under divisorial Bridgeland stability conditions. On the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at two general points, we characterize stability and semistability of a line bundle, or of its shift in the tilted heart, in terms of the three $(-1)$-curves. We also prove that, on any smooth projective surface, the pushforward of a torsion-free sheaf of rank $1$ on an integral curve of nonpositive self-intersection is stable for every divisorial stability condition.

papers.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over quartic fields
papers.abstract:
Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a quartic field $K$. By the Mordell-Weil theorem, $E(K)$ is a finitely generated group. We determine all the possibilities for the torsion group $E(K)_{tor}$ where $K$ ranges over all quartic fields $K$ and $E$ ranges over all elliptic curves over $K$. We show that there are no sporadic torsion groups, or in other words, that all torsion groups either do not appear or they appear for infinitely many non-isomorphic elliptic curves $E$.
  Proving this requires showing that numerous modular curves $X_1(m,n)$ have no non-cuspidal degree $4$ points. We deal with almost all the curves using one of 3 methods: a method for the rank 0 cases requiring no computation; the Hecke sieve, a local method requiring computer-assisted computations; and the global method, an argument for the positive rank cases also requiring no computation. We deal with the handful of remaining cases using ad hoc methods.

papers.title: Collision Primes of J₀(23): Forced Congruences, Exceptional Local Factors, and a Pre-Registered Test of the Murty–Van Hirtum Constant
papers.abstract: Let \(f\) be the weight-two newform of level \(23\), with coefficient field \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\). We call a prime \(p\neq 2,23\) a collision prime when \(a_p(f)\in\mathbb{Z}\), equivalently when its two Galois-conjugate Hecke eigenvalues coincide. We establish congruence restrictions at collision primes: \(a_p(f)\equiv p+1\pmod{11}\), while its parity is determined by the Frobenius class of \(p\) in the Hilbert class field of \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-23})\). Consequently, \(a_p(f)\bmod 22\) is determined by \(p\). We also prove a mod-four congruence for primes represented by the principal binary quadratic form and formulate a further mod-four conjecture supported by 1,187,172 tested cases without exception. For the quantitative distribution of collisions, we investigate exceptional local factors using explicit hypothesized Galois-image models at \(3\) and \(11\), retaining an empirical factor at \(2\). A pre-registered initial model is rejected by the data. A revised model, frozen before evaluation on a held-out range, predicts 914.9 collisions against 909 observed between \(2\times10^7\) and \(6\times10^7\). The resulting heuristic asymptotic constant is approximately \(4.864\). The paper distinguishes proved statements, conditional image-model calculations, computational tests, and unresolved conjectures. Reproducibility materials are publicly available.

papers.title: Completing the Kim–Kim–Oh Classification of Minimal-Rank $n$-Universal Lattices for $2\le n\le 8$
papers.abstract: A positive-definite integral lattice is $n$-universal if it represents every positive-definite integral lattice of rank $n$. We complete the classification of minimal-rank $n$-universal lattices for $2\le n\le 8$ by resolving the three cases left open by Kim, Kim, and Oh. We show that $I_3\perp A_1\perp A_2$ and $I_3\perp A_2\perp\langle 3\rangle$ are $3$-universal, whereas $I_6\perp A_2$ is not $5$-universal.

papers.title: Differential forms and Brauer classes in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study $p$-torsion Brauer classes in positive characteristic arising from differential forms. We relate this construction to the Brauer group of supersingular K3 surfaces and analyze the contribution of these classes to the Brauer-Manin obstruction. As an application, we examine the Brauer-Manin set of supersingular K3 surfaces and of varieties admitting many differential forms.

papers.title: Dirac reduction algebra
papers.abstract: There is a homomorphism of associative superalgebras from the enveloping algebra of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ to the Weyl-Clifford superalgebra $A(2n|n)$ with $2n$ even Weyl algebra generators and $n$ odd Clifford algebra generators. Under this homomorphism, the positive odd root vector $x\in\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is sent to the Dirac operator $\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu\in A(2n|n)$ and generates a left ideal $I$. The corresponding reduction (super)algebra, denoted $Z_n$, is the normalizer of $I$ in $A(2n|n)$ modulo $I$. By construction, $Z_n$ acts on the space of all Clifford algebra-valued polynomial solutions to the (massless) Dirac equation. This setting goes back to Zhelobenko, who described generators of this reduction algebra and commutation relations among them. In this paper, we find a complete presentation of (a localization of) this so-termed Dirac reduction algebra, with full proofs. We give a closed formula for products of the raising operators in the reduction algebra and use it to write down explicitly the polynomial solutions to the Dirac equation in $n$-dimensional flat spacetime that they generate. Finally, we show that for $n\neq 2$ the space of polynomial solutions is irreducible over the reduction algebra tensored with the opposite Clifford algebra when $n$ is even, and is a direct sum of two irreducible submodules when $n$ is odd.

papers.title: Duality for Arithmetic $p$-adic Pro-\'etale Cohomology of Analytic Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that the arithmetic $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of smooth partially proper spaces over $K$ satisfies a duality, as conjectured by Colmez, Gilles and Nizio{\l}. We derive it from the geometric duality on the Fargues-Fontaine curve by Galois descent techniques of Fontaine.

papers.title: Exact Solutions to the Klein--Gordon Equation via Reduction Algebras
papers.abstract: Reduction algebras (also known as generalized Mickelsson algebras, Zhelobenko algebras, or transvector algebras) are well-studied associative algebras appearing in the representation theory of Lie algebras. In the 1990s, Zhelobenko noted that reduction algebras have a connection to field equations from physics, whereas Howe's study of dual pairs in the 1980s signifies that the link originated even earlier. In this paper, we revisit the simplest case of a massless scalar field, in arbitrary spacetime dimension $n\ge 3$ and arbitrary flat metric $\eta_{ab}$; the field equation then specializes to the Laplace equation and to the massless Klein--Gordon equation. The relevant reduction algebra comes from a representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ (technically, $\mathfrak{sp}_2$) by differential operators. We give a complete presentation of this reduction algebra. Its raising operators produce bosonic states $|a_1a_2\cdots a_\ell\rangle$, polynomial solutions of degree $\ell$ to the field equation, and we show that the natural bilinear form on these states is computed by symmetrizers built from the rational dynamical R-matrix. Along the way we give explicit formulas for the states, and a self-contained proof, for a general metric, of Zhelobenko's results that they span the polynomial solutions and that the solution space is an irreducible module over the reduction algebra.

papers.title: Expansion in powers of Suzuki groups
papers.abstract: In a companion paper, we proved that every $d$-generated direct power $G^m$ of a nonabelian finite simple group $G$, other than an alternating group or a Suzuki group, has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements whose normalized spectral gap is at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C$. Here, in an AI-generated addendum to that paper, the same is proved for the Suzuki groups $\mathrm{Sz}(q)$. The main step is that, for $m\le q^{1/100}$ and with probability tending to one as $q$ grows, a random pair of elements generates $\mathrm{Sz}(q)^m$ and gives a Cayley graph whose spectral gap is bounded below independently of $q$ and $m$. For $m=1$ this is a theorem of Breuillard, Green and Tao. The proof follows the method of Bourgain and Gamburd, with a growth theorem for $\mathrm{Sz}(q)^s$ whose constants do not depend on $s$.

papers.title: Finding most likely Delaunay triangulations of imprecise points is NP-hard
papers.abstract: For $n$ independent planar Gaussian sites, we seek the most probable Delaunay triangulation, specified by its labelled triangular faces. The search is NP-hard even for rational centres in general position and a fixed common isotropic covariance. Six triangulations can outrank the centre triangulation for four sites and at least $(n-1)!/2$ can do so for sufficiently large $n$. In one dimension, sorting the centres of independent Gaussians with common variance gives a Delaunay path with at least half the maximum probability in $O(n\log n)$ comparisons. In the plane, however, finding a triangulation with even half the maximum probability is NP-hard for independent standard Gaussian displacements. This hardness holds for every fixed fraction between zero and one, so a relative polynomial-time approximation scheme would imply $P=NP$. In both reductions, every qualifying triangulation from one call yields a maximum independent set of the input planar cubic graph. For Gaussian input, sampling finds, with probability at least $1-\delta$, a triangulation whose probability is within $\varepsilon$ of the maximum. Its running time is polynomial in the input bit length, $1/\varepsilon$ and $\log(1/\delta)$. Exact and constant-factor search for Delaunay triangulations remain NP-hard for fixed bounded rotation-invariant planar densities for which the logarithm of one plus the displacement length has a finite positive-order moment, and for fixed invertible linear images of these laws. This includes every fixed positive definite Gaussian covariance, uniform-ellipse and Cauchy noise, and laws without a positive moment of the displacement length. Bounded projection densities also suffice for some singular planar laws. For the convex hull, finding a most probable set of extreme labels is NP-hard for site-dependent isotropic Gaussian variances. Its complexity for a common variance remains open.

papers.title: Freeness of the square root of the inverse different
papers.abstract: Let (L/K) be a weakly ramified Galois extension of number fields of odd degree, with group (G), and let (\mathcal A_{L/K}) be the square root of its inverse different. We prove that (\mathcal A_{L/K}\simeq\mathbb Z[G]^{[K:\mathbb Q]}).

papers.title: Gene ologs: a categorical framework for Gene Ontology
papers.abstract: The Gene Ontology (GO) is the most widely used resource for the functional annotation of genes and gene products. It unifies biological knowledge across species through a dynamic, controlled vocabulary, and it is now primarily represented in the Web Ontology Language (OWL), a logic-based language that supports automated reasoning. Ologs (ontology logs), introduced by Spivak and Kent, offer a different language for knowledge representation, grounded in category theory: concepts are types, functional relationships are aspects, and declared equalities between paths are facts. Ologs come with features that are not part of the standard use of GO: path equations, universal constructions (products, coproducts, pullbacks and pushouts), a database reading in which instance data are set-valued functors, and functors with which ontologies can be compared and merged. In this work we take an initial step towards Gene ologs, i.e. ologs for GO. We fix conventions for reading GO terms as olog types, examine which GO relations can be represented as aspects and which must instead be represented as spans, illustrate each olog construction with GO examples, show that standard GO annotations and GO Causal Activity Models (GO-CAM) can be represented as olog instance data subject to checkable constraints, and describe how functors and pushouts can be used to compare and merge Gene ologs. We also discuss what ologs do not provide relative to OWL. We regard Gene ologs as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the OWL representation of GO.

papers.title: Global smoothing of singular Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study the problem of smoothing Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties with isolated Du Bois (equivalently, log canonical) lci singularities. For Fano varieties, we show that any such $Y$ admits a deformation to a Fano variety with only $1$-rational singularities, and if $Y$ has only non-$1$-rational hypersurface singularities, then $Y$ is smoothable. For Calabi-Yau varieties, we show first that any such $Y$ deforms to a Calabi-Yau with only $1$-Du Bois singularities. Moreover, if $Y$ has only non-$1$-Du Bois hypersurface singularities then $Y$ is smoothable. Both smoothing statements extend to lci singularities satisfying suitable local conditions. When we allow a Calabi-Yau to have $1$-liminal singularities, a global condition is needed, which we express in terms of the Hodge-Du Bois numbers of $Y$. These theorems recover and generalize results for threefolds of Friedman, Namikawa, Namikawa-Steenbrink, Gross, and Friedman-Laza. In higher dimensions, our results provide alternative smoothing conditions and also extend the work of Friedman-Laza from the case of rational hypersurface singularities to Du Bois lci singularities.

papers.title: Higher weighted Lucas sums and even q-beta values
papers.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the Lucas numbers and $B_j=\sum_{m\ge1}m^{2j-1}/L_{2m}$. At least one of $B_2,\ldots,B_{10}$ is linearly independent of $1,B_1$ over the rationals. The family contains infinitely many linearly independent values. More generally, at every positive real quadratic unit $q<1$ of norm one, the rational dimension of the even $q$-beta values through weight $A-1$, together with $1$, grows at least on the order of $\sqrt A$.

papers.title: How Many Cycle Lengths Can a Unique Quotient Require?
papers.abstract: Given two permutations \(A\) and \(B\), suppose there is just one finite dynamical system \(X\), up to isomorphism, whose direct product with \(A\) is \(B\). How many different cycle lengths can \(X\) have? For every sufficiently large \(k\) we construct a divisor with \(k\) cycle lengths and a target with exactly \(k+1\). Their unique quotient has asymptotically \(\tfrac12 k^2\log_2\log k\) distinct cycle lengths. Every one of these lengths is absent from the target. The divisor is fixed once \(k\) is chosen. Its cycles have lengths \(M/p\), where \(M\) is the product of the first \(k\) primes and \(p\) runs over those primes. The proof chooses a set containing almost all the first \(k\) primes. Each quotient cycle omits exactly two primes of this set. A congruence fixes the number of states assigned to each missing pair. Smaller primes then distinguish several forced cycle lengths within each pair.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Embeddings in Toric Geometry: Effectivity and Deformation Stability
papers.abstract: We study the deformation behavior of Kobayashi hyperbolic embeddings for complements of divisors in projective toric varieties. In the toric setting, the Zariski closure of an entire curve in a torus complement is a translate of an algebraic subtorus contained in that complement. This translates hyperbolicity questions into combinatorial conditions on lattice-point configurations of Newton polytopes. Building on a theorem of Tiba, which guarantees hyperbolic embedding for a general divisor under suitable facewise lattice conditions, we develop an effective refinement of his argument. We construct an explicit constructible bad locus in the coefficient parameter space, characterized by the presence of translated subtori in the divisor or its complement on a torus stratum, and use its proper Zariski closure as an exceptional locus. This description makes the exceptional set amenable to computation. Using this effectivity, we prove a deformation stability result: along any algebraic one-parameter family of divisors whose initial member avoids the exceptional locus, hyperbolic embedding fails for at most finitely many parameters. Under strengthened lattice-point hypotheses, we further exhibit distinguished one-parameter families for which hyperbolic embedding persists without any exceptional parameters. We also analyze deformations arising from diagonal torus reparametrizations. If the initial divisor lies outside $\mathcal Y$, the inverse image of $\mathcal Y$ under the similarity family is empty on the nondegenerate parameter domain, while the smallest possible degeneracy set of a rational similarity presentation is controlled by a multiplicative rank invariant of the scaling vector. Finally, we illustrate the theory through examples in projective spaces and Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: Independence of homogeneous GKM manifolds and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Let $G/H$ be a simply connected homogeneous space of maximal rank. Then the maximal torus $T$-action on $G/H$ equips it with a structure of a Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifold. We call the $T$-action $j$-independent if any $i\leq j$ pairwise distinct isotropy weights at a fixed point are linearly independent. Using weighted graphs, we show that the maximal independence of $G/H$ is $2$, $3$ or $n=\dim T$, and that the cases of $3$ or $n=\dim T$ correspond to some symmetric spaces of rank $>2$ by using the Lie bracket structure at the tangent space at identity coset. We classify all $4$-independent homogeneous spaces by studying the $3$- and $4$-cycles in the matroid of the respective root subsystem complement using Borel-de Siebenthal and Cartan classification results. In the classical $G$ cases our case study of maximal independence relies on signed weighted graphs, following the classical methods of Zaslavsky and Harari. In the exceptional simply laced $G$ cases we either present a $3$-cycle, or prove that there is none by reducing them only to those having a form $x+y=z$ for positive roots $x,y,z$ and find an affine hyperplane containing the respective root complement. As a corollary, using the results of Ayzenberg and Masuda, the lower-degree reduced rational cohomology groups of the orbit space $T\backslash G/H$ vanish.

papers.title: Integer-valued polynomials over a one-dimensional analytically irreducible local domain form a free module: Elliott's non-flatness conjectures fail
papers.abstract: In 2011 J. Elliott conjectured that the ring $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ of integer-valued polynomials is not flat over $D=\mathbf F_2[[T^2,T^3]]$, nor over $D=\mathbf F_2+T\mathbf F_4[[T]]$, and more generally that some local, Noetherian, one-dimensional, analytically irreducible domain has a non-flat $\operatorname{Int}(D)$. This spring H. Ma, with the reasoning system Rethlas, answered Problem 19 of Cahen, Fontana, Frisch and Glaz negatively, with a local domain whose normalization has two maximal ideals. We prove that Elliott's conjectures fail. If $D$ is a subring of a discrete valuation ring $V$ with finite residue field, and $D$ contains a nonzero ideal of $V$, then $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ is a free $D$-module. Consequently $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ is free for every one-dimensional analytically irreducible Noetherian local domain $D$. By Elliott's own theorems, the canonical maps $\operatorname{Int}(D)^{\otimes n}\to\operatorname{Int}(D^n)$ are then isomorphisms and $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ carries a unique compatible biring structure. For Elliott's two rings we write down the polynomials explicitly. The proof patches two free modules along the conductor square and uses a matrix identity of Whitehead and a theorem of Kaplansky. The proof was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). The corollary for analytically irreducible domains and the explicit examples were written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, which also checked the proof; Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked the whole note again. No human has checked this note.

papers.title: K-moduli with real coefficients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an algebraic K-stability theory (e.g. special test configuration theory and optimal destabilization theory) for log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs, and construct a proper K-moduli space to parametrize K-polystable log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs with some fixed invariants (e.g. dimension, volume, coefficients). All of these are well-known for log Fano $\mathbb Q$-pairs, and the strategy in this paper is trying to reduce the problems (in many cases) to $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case rather than rebuilding the whole program as in $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case.

papers.title: Kapranov $L_{\infty}[1]$ algebras
papers.abstract:
Given any K\"ahler manifold $X$, Kapranov discovered a nontrivial $L_\infty[1]$ algebra structure on $\Omega^{0,\bullet}_{X}(T^{1,0}X)$. Motivated by this result, we introduce the notion of an $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra, generalizing $L_\infty[1]$ algebras, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is a differential graded commutative algebra with unit. We extend standard notions such as quasi-isomorphism and linearization to this setting and establish a linearization theorem.
  As an application, we prove that any DG Lie algebroid $(\mathcal{L},Q_{\mathcal{L}})$ over a DG manifold $(\mathcal{M},Q)$ induces a distinguished isomorphism class of $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is the DG commutative algebra $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}),Q)$. Their unary bracket is $Q_{\mathcal{L}}$, while their binary bracket is a cocycle representative of the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid. All these isomorphic $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures are $\mathfrak{R}$-linearizable if and only if the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid vanishes. In contrast, the induced $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathbb{K}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$ are necessarily $\mathbb{K}$-linearizable, hence $\mathbb{K}$-homotopy abelian.

papers.title: Kim's universal octonary form over real quadratic orders
papers.abstract: Let \(R\) be a real quadratic order with fundamental totally positive unit \(\varepsilon\). Kim's octonary form is universal over \(R\) if and only if \(R=\Z[\varepsilon]\), or equivalently if the discriminant of \(R\) is \(T^2-4\) for an integer \(T\geq 3\). Building on recent work of Kala, Man, Visser, and Yatsyna, we determine the minimal universality criterion sets for classical and integer-valued lattices over these orders when \(T\) is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of twisted maps to smooth pairs
papers.abstract: We study moduli spaces of twisted maps to a smooth pair in arbitrary genus, and give geometric explanations for the known comparisons between orbifold and logarithmic Gromov--Witten invariants. We classify the irreducible components of the space of twisted maps to the universal target in terms of tropical data, and show that each is built from torsors under semi-abelian varieties coming from Jacobians of the domain curves. Natural morphisms between these spaces for different rooting parameters measure how each component grows: for rooting parameters sufficiently large and divisible, the growth is monomial, with exponent between $0$ and $\max(0,2g-1)$, and the main component is the only one with exponent $0$. In genus $1$ the virtual class is the fundamental class, which recovers the polynomiality results of Tseng and You. We conclude with geometric examples, beginning with Maulik's original genus $1$ example.

papers.title: Neural Learning of Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms: a Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: We combine neural learning and geometric diagnostics to investigate the rank and border rank of the \(3\times3\) matrix-multiplication tensor \(M_3\). Using the Bhattacharya--Mesner product, we derive \textsc{MatMulNet}, a differentiable architecture encoding bilinear maps. Constrained refinement yields a length-\(23\) numerical solution with machine-precision full-tensor residual and bounded decomposition weight. Along the explored length-\(22\) branch, the residual instead decreases as the gauge-invariant weight grows. This contrast supports \(R_{\mathbb R}(M_3)=23\) as a working hypothesis. A Laurent-parametrised extension probes border rank, giving a tentative, protocol-dependent motivation to investigate \(r=19\) and the adjacent \(r=18\) case. For \(M_4\), the same diagnostics distinguish bounded numerical solutions recovered from perturbed known schemes, structured residual plateaus, and weight-growing approximations, revealing the dependence of the search on initialisation. Together, the experiments connect approximation accuracy with decomposition growth and identify concrete targets for exact or certified investigation.

papers.title: On a definitition of slice regular algebraic varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a complete correspondence between irreducible slice regular algebraic sets and quasi prime radical right ideals in the ring of quaternionic slice regular polynomials. In particular we make use of the definition of quasi prime ideals to give a characterization of irreducibility of slice regular algebraic sets. More precisely, we show that if $I$ is a radical and quasi prime right ideal, then $\mathbb S_{V_c(I)}$, the symmetrization of $V_c(I)$, is an irreducible slice regular algebraic set, where $V_c(I)$ denotes the set of common zeros with commuting components of polynomials in $I$. Combining this fact with the results of one of our previous papers, we obtain that for $I$ radical, $V_c(I)$ is irreducible if and only if $I$ is quasi prime. We also find a complete characterization of quasi prime radical right ideals, proving that either they are completely prime or the radical of the symmetrization $S(J)$ of a completely prime right ideal $J$.

papers.title: On Some Diophantine Parameters of the Cyclic Torsion Subgroups of Odd Order of Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: For elliptic curves $ E $ over the rational number field $ \Q, $ based on Mazur's classical result, we give in this paper some explicit Diophantine parameters for their cyclic torsion subgroups $ E(\Q)_{\text{tors}} $ of odd order. This work is a continuation of the ones in ([Q1], [QZ1$\sim $2]). Such explicit form of parameters might be useful in calculating torsion subgroups of elliptic curves over higher degree number fields.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
papers.abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

papers.title: Parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields) on a formal principal bundle with parahoric structures. This generalizes the reduction theory due to Hukuhara-Levelt-Turrittin and Babbitt-Varadarajan in the case without parahoric structures [7], and Boalch's result in the case of regular singularity [14]. As applications, we first prove that a formal connection is intrinsically regular if and only if it is a parahoric formal connection, in combination with the works of Bremer-Sage [45] and Chen-Kamgarpour [20], providing various criteria for the regularity of formal connections. We then introduce a notion of relative regularity for formal connections and give criterions. Finally, we demonstrate a parahoric version of Frenkel-Zhu's Borel reduction theorem of formal connections [33].

papers.title: Rational Curves on Coindex 3 Fano Varieties
papers.abstract: We describe the moduli space of rational curves on smooth Fano varieties of coindex 3. For varieties of dimension 5 or greater, we prove the moduli space has a single irreducible component for each effective numerical class of curves. For varieties of dimension 4, we describe families of rational curves in terms of Fujita's $a$-invariant. Our results verify Lehmann and Tanimoto's Geometric Manin's Conjecture for all smooth coindex 3 Fano varieties over the complex numbers.

papers.title: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
papers.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

papers.title: Relation (IV) of Nakamura and Schneps holds on the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, with an application to the two elliptic points of the modular curve
papers.abstract: Nakamura and Schneps (2000) defined a subgroup of the profinite Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ by two relations, $(\mathrm{III}')$ and $(\mathrm{IV})$, that hold for Galois elements; they proved that it acts on the profinite mapping class groups of all surfaces, and left open whether it is all of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. We prove that $(\mathrm{IV})$ holds for every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. It follows that every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ is the product of a Galois element and an element of the group $\Lambda$ of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, which acts on the whole tower of pure mapping class groups by their formulas. As an application we study a character $\delta$ with values in $\mathbf F_2$, defined on the larger group given by the two- and three-cycle relations alone, which compares at level twelve how an element moves the two elliptic points of the modular curve. We prove that $\delta$ vanishes on the normalized elements of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, so that every character extending it and trivial on Galois elements is trivial on $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. The proofs use the theorem of Boggi and Zalesskii on finite $p$-subgroups of profinite completions, the action of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, and the theorem of Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki on the outer automorphisms of genus-zero configuration groups. Relation $(\mathrm{III}')$ is not touched. The mathematics was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode); it was checked by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, which wrote this text and rewrote several proofs, and by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max as second reader. No human has checked it.

papers.title: Resurgence of the finite-$N$ Curie--Weiss model: metastability, the spinodal, and Lee--Yang zeros
papers.abstract: We give a resurgent description of the Curie--Weiss (mean-field Ising) model at finite $N$ below the critical temperature in a magnetic field. We argue, modulo the standard identification of lateral thimble integrals with lateral Borel sums, that the partition function is the sum of exactly two sectors, the stable and the metastable phase. Each sector's $1/N$ series is factorially divergent, with its Borel singularity at its own free-energy barrier, and the two Stokes discontinuities cancel. As a result, the median Borel sums of the two series reproduce the exact partition function, which we confirm numerically to a relative error below $10^{-28}$ at $N=150$. Lateral resummation of the metastable series gives the imaginary part of the metastable free energy, with Langer's factor $\tfrac12$ appearing as a half-thimble. At distance $\delta$ below the spinodal field, the metastable singularity approaches the origin as $\tfrac{16}{3}\delta^{3/2}/\sqrt{\Phi_0'''(x_s)}$, where $\Phi_0(x)$ is the mean-field free-energy functional in the up-spin fraction $x$ and $x_s$ is the spinodal point. There we construct the two-point Chester--Friedman--Ursell uniform expansion, in which both lateral sums become $(\Bi\pm\ii\Ai)$ and $(\Bi'\pm\ii\Ai')$ combinations with contour-independent coefficients. Tested against an exact Hubbard--Stratonovich representation of the metastable sector, the sixth-order uniform expansion achieves a relative error below $7\times10^{-20}$ at $N=3200$ across the tested values $\zeta_{\mathrm{lin}}\in\{0.5,1,2,3,5\}$ of the linearized Airy variable. On the imaginary-field axis, an anti-Stokes line, the resummed two-phase transseries reproduces the exact Lee--Yang zeros at $N=40$, with absolute errors below $2.5\times10^{-18}$ for the zero nearest the real axis and below $3\times10^{-28}$ for the four farthest ones. The zero at fixed filling $s=(k+\tfrac12)\pi/N$ has a divergent $1/N$ expansion. We determine its first two coefficients by integral inversion and in closed form, express the third in terms of the next Laplace coefficient, and compute the series through order $N^{-30}$. Pad\'e poles of its Borel transform numerically approach the complex barrier action $\mathcal{A}$, where $\operatorname{Im}\mathcal{A} = s$ by construction. Its Borel--Pad\'e sum reproduces the exact zeros with absolute errors decreasing from $4\times10^{-9}$ at $N=24$ to $2\times10^{-34}$ at $N=328$; from $N\approx200$ onward, truncation at order $N^{-30}$ is the limiting factor.

papers.title: Seshadri Regions and the Asymptotic Shape of Multigraded Regularity
papers.abstract: We introduce the Seshadri region of a subvariety, a convex region packaging the classical Seshadri constants with respect to every line bundle simultaneously. We develop the theory of Seshadri regions as a measure of positivity along subvarieties and apply it to determine asymptotic Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for ideal powers and symmetric powers on smooth projective toric varieties.

papers.title: Short representations and counting with distinct odd unit fractions
papers.abstract: Every rational number $a/b$ in $(0,1)$ with $b$ odd is a sum of $O(1+\log\log b)$ distinct unit fractions with odd denominators. This gives the order of both the maximum and the mean minimum length at each odd denominator. For the representations of $1$ with exactly $k$ terms, we show that the double logarithm of their number has order $k$ along the odd integers. In fact, for each sufficiently large odd $k$, one can fix the first $k-2$ denominators and still obtain at least $\exp(\exp(ck))$ different endings. Each largest denominator in this family is divisible by all of the first $\lfloor\exp(ck)\rfloor$ odd primes. We also obtain doubly exponentially many possible largest denominators, each attained by doubly exponentially many representations of that length.

papers.title: Springer's 1951 conjecture on inverse coefficients settled: true at every odd order, false at every even order from four on
papers.abstract: Let $g(z)=z+b_1z^{-1}+b_2z^{-2}+\cdots$ be analytic and one-to-one in $|z|>1$, and let $G(w)=w+B_1w^{-1}+B_2w^{-2}+\cdots$ be its inverse near infinity. Fix $n\ge1$, and let $q$ be the least prime divisor of $n+1$. In 1951 Springer conjectured that, among all such $g$, the modulus of the inverse coefficient $B_n$ is largest when $g$ maps $|z|>1$ onto the complement of $q$ straight slits of equal length that issue from the origin at equal angles. At odd orders $n=2m+1$ the conjecture reads $|B_{2m+1}|\le C_m$, where $C_m=(2m)!/(m!\,(m+1)!)$ is a Catalan number, with equality only for the maps $z+e^{i\theta}/z$. This case was known for $m\le 7$ and for odd functions $g$, and further cases through $m=16$ have been reported. We prove this inequality and the equality statement for every $m$ and every $g$. More precisely, $B_{2m+1}$ lies in the closed disk with center $-2^{-m}C_m\, b_1^{m+1}$ and radius $(1-2^{-m})C_m$. The proof follows the inverse function along a Loewner evolution and bounds its coefficients, by induction, by those of the inverses of the slit maps $z+t/z$. For $n=2$ the conjecture is a classical theorem of Schiffer and Golusin. For every even $n\ge 4$ the conjecture is false. When $n+1$ is not divisible by $3$, this failure is due to Chang, Schiffer and Schober (1981) and Kuznetsov (1988). We establish the failure at the remaining orders $n=8,14,20,\ldots$, and we give explicit counterexamples for every even $n\ge4$. For even $n\ge4$ the maximum of $|B_n|$ is, to our knowledge, unknown, but it is at least a positive constant times $2^nn^{-3/2}$, whereas the conjectured bound is only $2/(n+1)$ when $n+1$ is prime. These results are verified in Lean.

papers.title: Tensor ideals of abelian type and quantum groups
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of tensor ideals in linear rigid monoidal categories that are kernels of linear monoidal functors to abelian monoidal categories. We develop general methods and apply them to the category of tilting modules over quantum groups as well as to some representation categories of finite groups. In an appendix on Duflo involutions in monoidal categories, we make a connection between Duflo involutions in the affine Weyl group and tensor ideals for quantum groups, and prove some of Lusztig's conjectures for arbitrary Coxeter groups, at equal parameters, without invoking the boundedness hypothesis.

papers.title: The 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups
papers.abstract: We determine the 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups over S^4.

papers.title: The boundary structure of the maximum likelihood eliminant of $3\times3\times3$ tables
papers.abstract: The maximum likelihood estimate of the no-three-way interaction model for $3\times3\times3$ contingency tables is an algebraic function of the table $n$, and each fitted cell is a root of a polynomial $E(x;n)$ of degree $511$ in $x$, the maximum likelihood degree of the model. We describe the structure of this polynomial at the boundary. Conjecturally, the leading and constant coefficients factor completely into $103$ linear forms in the counts with coefficients $\pm1$: two-way margins, sums over pairs of complementary boxes, a staircase set, boxes with a full side, the total, and differences of two boxes. We explain each exponent as the Euler characteristic of a boundary stratum, satisfying the conservation identity $870=511+359$ between the $60$ vanishing strata, the interior torus, and the $43$ blow-up strata. On the hyperplane of a form, critical points of the likelihood escape along the coefficient vector of the form, either onto a facet, where the count is the maximum likelihood degree of a model with structural zeros, or into the zero-margin locus of a box, where the count is the Euler characteristic of an explicit residual variety. Up to symmetry, under the assumption that escaping branches move along these vectors, these eight types are the only forms with coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ having this property. The valuations force factors of the coefficients, and near each hyperplane the eliminant splits into the eliminant of the surviving roots and a boundary eliminant on the stratum, which share a collision discriminant at their meeting degree. We reduce the boundary system on each of the $325$ boundary hyperplanes (under all table symmetries) to an explicit eliminant: in closed form for the $99$ facets of exponent one, the junction branch of valuation $-2$ on $N=0$, the $81$ difference forms of exponent four (where the boundary system decouples into two univariate quadratics), the $27$ boxes $B_{223}$ of exponent six, and the $81$ box pairs $P_{112},P_{122}$ of exponent seventeen; for the $9$ slabs, to the $29$ critical points of a master function on the flow space of $K_{3,3}$; and for the $27$ margins, to the $169$ critical points of the model with structural zeros. While the $103$ active forms with $\lambda_{111}\neq0$ send escaping roots to $0$ or $\infty$, on the $222$ neutral boundary hyperplanes with $\lambda_{111}=0$ the escaping roots converge to finite nonzero values of $p_{111}$, so that for $n_0$ on such a hyperplane, $E(x;n_0)$ factors in $\Q(n_0)[x]$. Across all $189$ symmetry types of pairs of active boundary forms, the numbers of jointly escaping branches coincide with the end-coefficient exponents of the boundary eliminants and yield a two-regime restriction law for every cofactor $Q_k$, consisting of same-side codimension-two tents and opposite-side interior plateaus. Finally, we conjecture that the eliminant is the residual resultant of the margin conditions on the no-three-way interaction toric variety: for a generic scaling of the model, the eliminant has degree $2{,}457$, and as the scaling tends to the uniform one, $1{,}946$ of its roots escape along the same vectors into the zero-margin loci of the four box types. Some of these statements are proved, some only under stated hypotheses, and the others are conjectures supported by exact, modular, and numerical computation.

papers.title: The lattice of rainbow bases
papers.abstract: Let \(E\) be the labelled union of \(n\) bases of an \(n\)-dimensional vector space over a field. We determine the integer lattice generated by the incidence vectors of its rainbow bases. It consists of the integer vectors with equal colour sums and component sums equal to the common colour sum times the component ranks, and it is saturated. In particular, the all-one vector is an integer combination of these incidence vectors. Over every field, for every sufficiently large integer \(k\), the multiset containing \(k\) copies of each label can be partitioned into \(kn\) rainbow bases.

papers.title: The question of Anderson and Ihara on the pro-p Galois action on the projective line minus three points, at every prime satisfying Vandiver's conjecture
papers.abstract: Ihara showed that the kernel of the outer action of the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb Q$ on the pro-$p$ fundamental group of the projective line minus three points cuts out a field contained in the maximal pro-$p$ extension of $\mathbb Q(\mu_p)$ unramified outside $p$, and Anderson and Ihara asked whether the two fields are equal. Sharifi proved that they are equal at odd regular primes if the Deligne--Ihara conjecture holds, and Brown proved that conjecture. We prove the equality at every odd prime $p$ for which the plus part of the Iwasawa module of $p$-class groups of the cyclotomic tower is finite. This holds whenever $p$ does not divide the class number of the real cyclotomic field $\mathbb Q(\mu_p)^+$, which is Vandiver's conjecture at $p$; by the computation of Hart, Harvey and Ong the equality therefore holds at every odd prime below $2^{31}$. At an irregular prime the Galois group in question has generators that the regular case does not have. The theorems of Fukaya--Kato and Wake--Wang-Erickson on Sharifi's symbol map show that cup products of cyclotomic units generate the relevant second cohomology at every finite level, and we prove that this forces the images of the new generators to have poles that separate all words. The mathematics and the proofs were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high checked the deduction from Vandiver's conjecture and the present text of Sections 4 to 6 step by step, with the theorems of Fukaya--Kato and Wake--Wang-Erickson read at the places cited; Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max edited the text, wrote its first two sections and refereed Sections 3 to 6. No human has checked it.

papers.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
papers.abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [arXiv:1408.3694,arXiv:1602.00654]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [arXiv:1803.04155] and the other in [arXiv:2110.11099], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [arXiv:2106.11587].

papers.title: The universal Euler characteristic and Burnside group for definable groupoids
papers.abstract:
We introduce the universal Euler characteristic of orbit space definable groupoids, a class of groupoids containing cocompact proper Lie groupoids as well as translation groupoids associated to proper definable group actions. We show that every additive and multiplicative invariant of orbit space definable groupoids with an additional local triviality hypothesis arises as a ring homomorphism applied to the universal Euler characteristic. This in particular includes the $\Gamma$-orbifold Euler characteristic introduced by the first and third authors when $\Gamma$ is a finitely presented group.
  For definable groupoids, where the object and arrow spaces as well as the structure maps are definable, we also introduce a Burnside group which is an analog of the classical Burnside ring associated to compact Lie groups and, for a transitive groupoid with compact isotropy, admits a partial multiplication.

papers.title: Theories of bundles with additional homotopy conditions
papers.abstract: A homotopy between two amplified special unitary bundles and a trivialization of a tensor product give two different finite-dimensional classifying spaces. For coprime ranks $k,l>1$ the first space is a biquotient of $\SU(kl)$ and the second is a homogeneous matrix Grassmannian. We distinguish the two manifolds for every such pair by their first Pontryagin classes. For $(k,l)=(2,3)$ their eighth integral cohomology groups have orders $3$ and $21$, respectively. The same amplification maps define a dimension-drop algebra on a labelled simplex. Its skeletal filtration gives a weighted cellular complex and computes $K_0$, $K_1$ and the unit when the vertex labels have greatest common divisor one. We also compute both groups for triangles with arbitrary vertex labels.

papers.title: Topological Frobenius algebras
papers.abstract: We define in a graded and topologized setting the notions of unital/counital/biunital infinitesimal anti-symmetric bialgebras and coFrobenius bialgebras and discuss their algebraic properties. We also define in this setting the notion of a 2D open-closed TQFT. We illustrate these structures with old and new examples of geometric origin that arise in contexts as varied as symplectic topology, string topology, manifold topology, and quantum homology. The underlying vector spaces, which are typically infinite dimensional, belong to a class of topological vector spaces known as Tate vector spaces.

papers.title: Topology, Hyperbolicity, and the Shafarevich Conjecture for Complex Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: This survey presents recent developments concerning the Shafarevich conjecture, non-abelian Hodge theories, hyperbolicity, and the topology of complex algebraic varieties, as well as the interplay among these areas. More precisely, we present the main ideas and techniques involved in the linear versions of the following conjectures: the Shafarevich conjecture, the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture, Koll\'ar's conjecture on the holomorphic Euler characteristic, the de Oliveira-Katzarkov-Ramachandran conjecture, and Campana's nilpotency conjecture. In addition, we discuss characterizations of the hyperbolicity of complex quasi-projective varieties via representations of their fundamental groups, together with the generalized Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture in the presence of a big local system.

papers.title: VP $\neq$ VNP over every field
papers.abstract: We prove that every arithmetic circuit that computes the permanent of an $m\times m$ matrix over the reals has more than $m^{c(\log m)^{1/3}}$ gates, for some constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $m$. The same bound holds over every field of characteristic other than two and, for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial in place of the permanent, the same bound holds over every field. Hence $\mathrm{VP}\ne\mathrm{VNP}$ over every field. This is the algebraic analogue of the conjecture $\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}$, but it does not settle that conjecture. Algebraic circuits must work for all inputs in the field and its extensions -- not just 0 and 1 -- thus our superpolynomial bound does not apply to Boolean circuits. The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model and has been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Weighted distribution of residual indices and the contribution of higher-degree primes
papers.abstract: The residual index at a prime ideal of good reduction counts the cosets of the reduced subgroup in the multiplicative residue group. For a fixed finitely generated group of rank \(r\) in a number field, we estimate index frequencies up to norm \(X\), uniformly over conditions on the Frobenius action on residue fields in a fixed finite Galois extension. Adjoin roots of unity and radicals of the generators to this extension. If the nontrivial zeta zeros of the resulting fields have real parts uniformly below \(r/(r + 1)\), the sum of absolute frequency errors weighted by small powers of the index admits a power saving. Model moments are finite for positive orders below \(r\). Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, empirical moments converge to them for positive orders below \((r - 1)/(r + 2)\). For rational generators in a nontrivial finite Galois extension of the rationals, we give an unconditional lower bound for the contribution of higher-degree ideals to the mean above any fixed index cutoff. This contribution diverges in rank one. For two rank-three groups over the Gaussian rationals, the sum of squared indices divided by \(X^{3/2}/\log X\) has lower limit at least \(329/648\). This growth exceeds the scale in the literal form of Ambrose’s prime-ideal heuristic.

papers.title: When is the Gohberg–Krupnik (1992) lower bound for aI+bH sharp? Exactly when Re(ab̄) = 0, for 1.2336… ≤ p ≤ 5.2807…, p ≠ 2
papers.abstract: Let $P_+$ and $P_-$ be the Riesz projections on the complex space $L^p(\mathbb T)$, $1<p<\infty$, onto the nonnegative and the negative frequencies, and let $H=-i(P_+-P_-)$, so that $aI+bH=\alpha P_++\beta P_-$ with $\alpha=a-ib$ and $\beta=a+ib$. Gohberg and Krupnik gave a lower bound for $\|aI+bH\|_p$, and Hollenbeck, Kalton and Verbitsky (2003) remarked that it is not sharp in general. We characterize when it is sharp. For $p\ne2$ and $\alpha\ne0$ the bound is not sharp whenever the ratio $\beta/\alpha$ is not real, and it is sharp whenever $\beta/\alpha$ is real and nonpositive. There is an explicitly defined $p_0\approx1.2336026$ such that the bound is sharp for every real ratio exactly when $p_0\le p\le p_0/(p_0-1)$; outside this interval it is not sharp for any real ratio below and sufficiently close to $1$. For $1<p<2$ and each real ratio $\lambda=\beta/\alpha\in(0,1)$ we give an exact criterion: an inequality on the positive real axis, together with the condition that $\lambda$ be smaller than an explicit threshold depending on $p$; the symmetries $\alpha\leftrightarrow\beta$ and $p\leftrightarrow p'$, where $p'=p/(p-1)$, cover the remaining real ratios and exponents. For $1<p<p_0$ the bound is sharp for all $\lambda$ near $0$, and on a band of intermediate ratios the outcome of the criterion is known only in part. The cases of $H$ itself, of a single projection and of $p=2$ are classical. We do not determine the norm where the bound is not sharp. The proof is computer-assisted and uses rigorous interval arithmetic on compact domains. The classification has also been proved in the Lean proof assistant, with the interval computations and two cited theorems (the Hollenbeck–Verbitsky norm of $P_+$ and Cole's theorem) taken as given.
